reviews.name: Romeo & Juliet (Delacorte Theater)
reviews.text: This is one of two Shakespearean statues positioned in front of the Shakespeare in the Park theatre, and they’re both just lovely.

reviews.name: The Family Sculpture (Bleecker Playground)
reviews.text: A lovely statue showing how two unstable adults can be stabilized into one cohesive unit when there’s a kid in the middle.

reviews.name: Bow Bridge & The Lake (Central Park)
reviews.text: Central Park has no shortage of beautiful bridges, and the Bow Bridge is one of that set. You can get a nice view of downtown behind the bridge from The Ramble.

reviews.name: Carnegie Hall
reviews.text: Carnegie Hall is one of the preeminent concert venues in the country, if not the world, and you can almost feel the grandeur in the halls. I was lucky enough to see Gustavo Dudamel conduct Tosca here, and will certainly try to return soon.

reviews.name: Oak Bridge
reviews.text: A simple bridge at the north end of The Lake which provides a nice, tree-framed view of the surrounding area

reviews.name: The Ramble
reviews.text: One of the greener and more heavily forested areas of Central Park, which can give this northerly portion a spookier vibe, especially when it’s dark or foggy

reviews.name: Hustle on George
reviews.location: Ground Floor/403 George St, Sydney NSW 2000, Australia
reviews.text: Really good oat chai lattes, and some great brew coffee. This is one of the only coffee shops open at 5am, and this was just perfect for me.

reviews.name: Hustlers.Syd
reviews.location: LG, 24 York St, Sydney NSW 2000, Australia
reviews.text: I came to Hustlers. for a work event, and we ordered drinks and a whole variety of starters and entrees and everything was great. While this place is a bit on the higher end, the quality is certainly on the higher end as well.

reviews.name: Mann med liten håndbevegelse
reviews.text: People, walking, without their clothing. Like a nightmare you had that one time

reviews.name: Edvard Grieg
reviews.text: Grieg was an impressive composer, it’s even more impressive how much he accomplished without any elbows.

reviews.name: Glory, glory with crutches
reviews.text: Good art makes one feel something, and Glory certainly evokes a feeling

reviews.name: National Monument for Victims of War 1940-45
reviews.text: What exactly is going on here, and why does it represent what Norway did in the Second World War? It leaves one with a lot of questions

reviews.name: Politihesten Tor
reviews.text: Didn’t know that this horse was here and just stumbled upon it. A wonderful surprise

reviews.name: Instalacja Jayco
reviews.text: Geometric art which has a certain charm to it

reviews.name: Statue of Franklin D. Roosevelt
reviews.text: The American president is plopped atop the hill, with an eternally nice view, fit for a quadruple elected man.

reviews.name: George C. Marshall
reviews.text: Yes, evidently that is George C. Marshall stood at the base of the hill. Awkwardly out of the way, why is he here?

reviews.name: Peter Jansen Wessel (Tordenskiold)
reviews.text: Certainly a man that gives off pirate energy

reviews.name: Scuba diver statue
reviews.text: This statue sits ready to plunge into the water at any moment. It’s simply perfect for the pier

reviews.name: Untuned Bell
reviews.text: Very, very easy to miss at first. You can control the bell with a pedal on the ground.

reviews.name: Rådhusplassen
reviews.text: This pier is where you’ll catch some of the boat tours of the fjords. It’s also the back side of the stunning City Hall building, which has a nice view of the water. There’s also a number of statues around the area.

reviews.name: Oslo City Hall
reviews.text: Despite City Hall being closed when I visited, the building is just spectacular, and still well worth visiting. Each face is unique, with the best faces being the one from the water, and the one with the clock, in my opinion.

reviews.name: Nordraaks plass
reviews.text: Absolutely one of the coolest small parks in the city, if not the whole Nordics. There are giant dragon statues, chained up for our protection.

reviews.name: Dronning Sonja
reviews.text: For the Royal Funeral, all of the Royal statues across the country had flowers placed on them, but I don’t think anyone got more than Dronning Sonja. She was absolutely covered.

reviews.name: Dronning Maud
reviews.text: Not quite the most prominently featured statue in the Slottenspark, but Maud is located in one of the nicer wooded areas. Maud is depicted in the typical Norwegian style here.

reviews.name: Karl Johan Monument
reviews.text: Karl Johan sits high on his horse, towering above on a pedestal, facing the Palace. At the time of the Royal Funeral, the whole area was covered in flowers and flags in respect to the late King. …

reviews.name: The Royal Palace
reviews.text: Though the Palace is currently closed, there are still ceremonies held on the Palace grounds, which are open to the public. The Royal Funeral was held here, and the King lied in wake for a period prior.

reviews.name: Slottsparken
reviews.text: Slottsparken is the multiblock-sized park that surrounds the royal palace. There’s a pathway which has a series of modern art items along it, and a few more lined by trees. Royal ceremonies are held here, including the recent Royal Funeral (pictured)

reviews.name: Aanerud Bakeri Oslo
reviews.text: A small, lovely bakery. Aanerud Bakeri is located down a side street, a bit outside of downtown. The pastries were fantastic, you can skip the drip coffee.

reviews.name: Oslo lufthavn
reviews.text: A perfectly fine airport with a decent variety of lighter food options in the International terminal, and a broader selection in the Main terminal area. …

reviews.name: Qantas International First Lounge Sydney
reviews.location: Sydney Airport, Terminal 1 Departure Plaza, Mascot NSW 2020, Australia
reviews.text: I stopped by the Qantas First Class Lounge one morning, and was treated like a princess. They made a great breakfast, which came out quickly, and then there were other areas to charge my devices and chill out before my flight

reviews.name: Sydney Airport
reviews.text: I quite enjoyed flying out of Sydney Airport. I was in First Class on American Airlines (for work) and the Qantas lounge was very phenomenal, I had such a good breakfast there. The rest of the airport had all of the amenities that you need.

reviews.name: Menya City Japanese Noodle Bar
reviews.text: I love Menya City; they’re quick, reasonably priced, and very tasty. The ramen was much better than the katsu.

reviews.name: Google Sydney - One Darling Island
reviews.location: 1 Darling Island Rd, Pyrmont NSW 2009, Australia
reviews.text: I’ve visited this Sydney office twice now, and while it’s not the largest office, it does have its charm. The parking situation definitely doesn’t seem ideal for the people based out of here, but as a visitor that was no bother to me

reviews.name: Life From A Suitcase
reviews.text: Love the sentiment of the statue, and the execution is certainly fine as well

reviews.name: Windjammers
reviews.text: Ripping statue with a truly nautical view of the downtown skyline.

reviews.name: Martin Place
reviews.text: Sydney’s central business district is littered with giant, majestic, parliament-style buildings, and Martin Place is one of this set. Just stunning on its own, but somehow out of place in its current home

reviews.name: Edward VII
reviews.text: Edward VII is regally and royally presented on his horse. My main complaint with this statue is how hard it is to reach it, and how unfriend it is to pedestrians

reviews.name: K H A O • S O I - カ オ • ソ ー イ
reviews.location: Level 2/73-75 Liverpool St, Sydney NSW 2000, Australia
reviews.text: I love Khao Soi, it’s one of my favorite Thai dishes. I’ve been to Chiang Mai, in northern Thailand, where the dish comes from. While the Khao Soi here was fine, it was quite unique in a way that I didn’t love. I’ve never had one so spicy. I often love spice, but with Khao Soi’s pickled taste profile, it just wasn’t my favorite combo.

reviews.name: Hyatt Regency Sydney
reviews.text: Set right on Cockle Bay, the Hyatt Regency is a very nice business hotel. I’ve stayed here twice, and both times the rooms were quite large and well stocked. As always, I prefer a usable mini-fridge to one that’s trying to sell me products.

reviews.name: Chinatown Sydney
reviews.text: Chinatown doesn’t occupy that many blocks, but there is a very high density of business, and two arches to boot.

reviews.name: Sydney Souvenirs
reviews.location: PADDY’s MARKET Cnr Thomas &, Stall 460 Hay St, Haymarket NSW 2000, Australia
reviews.text: In terms of vibes, Sydney Souvenirs’ was immaculate. No notes. And no comments on the products themselves.

reviews.name: Golden Water Mouth
reviews.text: I guess the tree carries some auspiciousness in bark, released by touch; but for the metal fencing, forbidding such an inquiry.

reviews.name: Sydney's Water Features - Sydney Culture History Walks
reviews.text: This one must’ve been under construction when I visited because it was all fenced off. I barely knew it was a monument

reviews.name: Hay St Market
reviews.location: Shop R1.05/13 Hay St, Haymarket NSW 2000, Australia
reviews.text: An indoor market comprised of a maze of restaurants, bakeries, bars, and coffee shops describes just a single portion of Hay St Market. Wander deeper and you’ll find more kitschy, touristy shops with more of a bazaar vibe. The place is way more expansive than one suspects.

reviews.name: AG LEGO® Certified Store Sydney, Pitt St Mall – World’s Largest LEGO® Certified Store
reviews.location: entry is Via, 400 George Street, Pitt Street Mall, Sydney NSW 2000, Australia
reviews.text: This store claims to be the largest LEGO store in the world, and I find that a bit surprising, but sure it’s quite sizable and has a lot of the iconic brick company’s partnerships on display. It’s a fun place to stop while exploring the capital’s downtown.

reviews.name: Royal Clock
reviews.text: Queen Victoria Building has two impressive clocks, and the Royal Clock is the bulkier, more castle-resembling one. It’s got its charm, don’t get me wrong, but it’s definitely the lesser of the pair.

reviews.name: Great Australian Clock
reviews.text: There are two tiered clocks hanging from Queen Victoria Building and the Great Australian Clock appears to tell the story of the country/continent. The clock has so many details, the longer you inspect it, the more you get from it

reviews.name: Queen Victoria Building
reviews.text: The central business district of Syndey has a number of stunning, imperial buildings, and the Queen Victory stands alone as the singular best. From the glass panel on the windows, to the two giant, ornate clocks that hang in either hall, to the historical note in the top floor, this mall has a lot to see apart from the modern day stores.

reviews.name: Athena
reviews.text: Small, simple, and elegant, I really enjoyed this statue, and found its existence additive to the city’s beauty

reviews.name: The Strand Arcade
reviews.text: Sydney’s downtown should be known for its stunning buildings, and The Strand Arcade, one of many similar arcades, stands near the very top of the class. A tall, straight, singular hall with colorful, slanted, angular panels on the roof, and red carpeting and accenting provide a wonderful visual.

reviews.name: Sydney Arcade
reviews.text: There’s a few arcades (in the British sense, meaning a long covered building) in Sydney, but the eponymous one is definitely not the top one. Potentially the LEGO store is the most notable thing about this building, apart from the lovely building itself.

reviews.name: Cenotaph
reviews.text: Quite the beautiful monument, one of many in this area, which has an entire pedestrian-only street devoted to it. There were plentiful fresh wreaths when I visited, the area was extremely well kept

reviews.name: Royal Australian Regiment Memorial
reviews.location: Regimental Square, 339A George St, Sydney NSW 2000, Australia
reviews.text: Not a giant monument, in stature, but still an impactful one. You’re just walking around the central business district and suddenly you stumble upon it

reviews.name: Rabbit woman, Dogman, vespa and coffee
reviews.location: Australia Square, 264 George St, Sydney NSW 2000, Australia
reviews.text: A lovely statue, a part of a series located in major cities around the work. It does appear that Rabbitwoman was originally holding something (maybe a coffee cup) which is now gone.

reviews.name: Sirius Cannon
reviews.text: This is actually a display in two parts: first the more obvious anchor, which is set off the ground, and then the cannon placed outwards, almost to intimidate oneself not to speak ill of the mediocre anchor

reviews.name: Sirius Anchor
reviews.text: Quite the large anchor is affixed onto a bit of ground, which itself is presented as a bit of art. Nah

reviews.name: Thomas Sutcliff Mort
reviews.text: Ol Tom is situated way up high, leaning on something of a pedestal as he gazes down on the masses

reviews.name: Obelisk of Distances
reviews.text: This obelisk almost taunts the reader in saying, “I bet you can’t make it to all of these far off locations”. And one day I hope to return to prove this monument wrong

reviews.name: Principal Road Marker
reviews.text: It’s a fine obelisk, and truly one of the finer monuments in Macquarie Place Park, but does an obelisk evoke roads? Maybe it’s a literal representation of a road

reviews.name: Macquarie Place Park
reviews.text: A very small park, but it rises above its smaller stature by being jam packed full of monuments, each fairly interesting in its own regard.

reviews.name: Bonds of Friendship
reviews.text: I did knot get this piece of art

reviews.name: Second World War Servicewomen Memorial
reviews.location: Jessie Street Gardens, 1-29 Loftus St, Sydney NSW 2000, Australia
reviews.text: A statue recognizing the unsung and so oft unrecognized heroes of the second world war.

reviews.name: Jessie Street Gardens
reviews.text: The tiniest of greeneries, set entirely between giant skyscrapers, and filled with monuments. Jessie Street Gardens is many things, but hardly a garden (in the American sense)

reviews.name: Moore Steps
reviews.text: One of the staircases that’ll get you down to the water portion of Circular Quay. Nothing spectacular but it does get the job done.

reviews.name: Dorothea Mackellar Writers Walk Plaque
reviews.text: Quotes from famous Australians and visitors to the island continent are featured all around Circular Quay in circular golden plaques in the pavement

reviews.name: Circular Quay Wharf
reviews.text: The main waterfront area with the Opera House. It’s a great place to get some photos taken. Also, look down, as there’s a series of writers featured in little circles

reviews.name: Tim Hortons
reviews.location: 6301 Silver Dart Dr Terminal 1, Mississauga, ON L4V 1R9, Canada
reviews.text: This Tim Hortons has a picture of Tim Horton in his hockey get-up. In decade of visiting the Tim Hortons chain, I never knew that it was named after a real guy.

reviews.name: The Happy Tummy Bar & Grill
reviews.text: A fine place for dinner, I had a bacon cheeseburger here and it was fine. I’d definitely come back and try the wings and poutine

reviews.name: Yellowknife Liquor Store
reviews.text: A very well stocked liquor store, with drinks from all over Canada and the world. I was especially appreciative that they carried nice ice wines from Niagara

reviews.name: Raccine Park
reviews.text: In the extremely flat Northwest Territories, Raccine Park contains something of a hill, which has been developed with a memorial

reviews.name: Bush Pilots Monument
reviews.location: 3513 Ingraham Dr #3511, Yellowknife, NT X1A 2E8, Canada
reviews.text: The highest point in Old Town Yellowknife offering sweeping views from the lake to the rest of the city. It’s not too much of a hike to get up there, though it can get fairly icy and slippery

reviews.name: Old Town Glassworks
reviews.location: 3510 McDonald Dr, Yellowknife, NT X1A 2H1, Canada
reviews.text: A lovely glass shop with tons of works made from recycled glasses. I also really appreciate the artwork and craftwork they had in the shop

reviews.name: Wing Freak
reviews.location: Nova Inn, 4401 Franklin Ave 3rd Floor, Yellowknife, NT X1A 1B5, Canada
reviews.text: A decent lunch option, the chicken was well portioned, filling, and tasty. Wing Freak’s strangely located on the 3rd floor of the Nova Inn, but worth the awkward eye contact with the person in the lobby

reviews.name: Yellowknife Visitor Centre
reviews.location: Centre Square Mall, 5014 50 St, Yellowknife, NT X1A 3R6, Canada
reviews.text: This isn’t the nicest spot in downtown Yellowknife, but there’s information and free maps here. They’ll also give you a little pin and a certificate for crossing the 60th parallel

reviews.name: ReLeaf NT
reviews.text: A decent shop. Broad supply and reasonable prices, all that you need. They also gave me popcorn which was pretty sweet

reviews.name: Yellowknife Public Library
reviews.location: 2nd Floor, Centre Square Mall, 5022 49 St, Yellowknife, NT X1A 3R8, Canada
reviews.text: The Library’s on the second floor of the mall, and features a small art collection with pieces around the floor. It’s a nice place to stop and support as a visitor

reviews.name: Northern Souvenirs & Gifts
reviews.text: A fair place to buy Canadian, Yellowknife, and Northwest Territory apparel and keepsakes. The store is very densely packed with goods

reviews.name: Trader’s Grill
reviews.text: Trader’s Grill is the restaurant within The Explorer Hotel, and it’s one of the nicest restaurants in Yellowknife. The Grilled Bison Ribeye was delicious and came with some nice sides. They also have Ice Wine for dessert. Trader’s has a …

reviews.name: The Explorer Hotel
reviews.text: I spent a single night at The Explorer Hotel, but I would stay long if I were in town for longer as everything was great: the restaurant, the rooms, the polar bear in the lobby - all of the essentials.

reviews.name: Bristol Monument
reviews.location: 361 Old Airport Rd, Yellowknife, NT X1A 3T2, Canada
reviews.text: One of the first things to greet you when you arrive in Yellowknife, the Bristol Monument sits high atop a hill above the welcome sign, with a brilliant and bright blue and red accented plane

reviews.name: welcome yellowknife sign
reviews.text: The Welcome Sign itself is pretty impressive, with the yellow knife and block text, how that pales in comparison to the large plane situated atop the hill next to it. All-in-all, this makes for one compelling stop

reviews.name: Lakeshore Co-op Gas Bar
reviews.location: 321 Old Airport Rd, Yellowknife, NT X1A 3T3, Canada
reviews.text: This Co-op is located decently close to the airport if you’re returning a rental car. The shop is very well stocked

reviews.name: Chan Lake Territorial Park
reviews.location: Fort Smith, Unorganized, NT X0E 0M0, Canada
reviews.text: An moderate vista, which proves to be a fine place to stop, when you need some respite. I’ll add, this had some of the deepest snowbanks that I found

reviews.name: Zhati Kue Friendship Centre
reviews.text: A community center with some very friendly people inside

reviews.name: Community Arbour
reviews.text: When I showed up at the Arbour there wasn’t a soul to be found, however, there was a decently well kept fire, with fresh wood next to the hearth. I appreciate whoever left this warm treat, but wish they’d stuck around

reviews.name: Our Lady of Providence
reviews.location: DehCho Dr, Fort Providence, NT X0E 0A7, Canada
reviews.text: An aesthetically crisp white church sat right on the water. It’s only open during the warmer months, so I can only assume the insulation isn’t the best

reviews.name: Kakisa River Territorial Park
reviews.location: Fort Smith, Unorganized, NT X0E 0L0, Canada
reviews.text: A stunning valley, covered in a sheet of sparkling white, with a simple - and seldom tread - bridge spanning it

reviews.name: Lady Evelyn Falls Territorial Park
reviews.text: Completely inaccessible and covered in snow

reviews.name: McNallie Creek Territorial Park Day Use Area
reviews.location: Fort Smith, Unorganized, NT X0E 0R1, Canada
reviews.text: Really spectacular looking falls when covered in snow. Nothing quite like those icicles dangling over the cliff

reviews.name: Woodland Wok & Grill
reviews.location: 66 Woodland Dr #8, Hay River, NT X0E 0R2, Canada
reviews.text: For lunch, it seemed like the buffet was the only option, which I was ok with. They food was fine, very much mall Chinese food, similar to what I grew up eating in The States

reviews.name: NWT Centennial Library
reviews.location: 75 Woodland Dr, Hay River, NT X0E 0R3, Canada
reviews.text: This is one of the nicest places to stop in Hay River, the NWT Centennial Library really is a nexus for local information. They also had some interesting local papers that they let me keep as a souvenir

reviews.name: Katlodeeche First Nation
reviews.location: Hay River 1, Hay River, NT X0E, Canada
reviews.text: Much easier to access in the months when the river is frozen. Just across the water from Hay River

reviews.name: The Forks
reviews.text: For half of the year, this portion of Hay River is frozen over, and it becomes an ice road connecting the two parts of the city across the water

reviews.name: Marine Transportation Services - Shipyard
reviews.location: 1 104 Ave, Hay River, NT X0E 0R2, Canada
reviews.text: In the winter, the ships freeze into the harbor, and really have a nice visual from the beach

reviews.name: Pumphouse Beach
reviews.text: A peculiar place to visit in the colder months, as all that you can see (over the parking lot’s snowbank), is endless, nearly perfectly untouched snow. Cool vista, kinda windy, you can skip this one

reviews.name: Parks Canada Fire Management Regional Fire Base
reviews.text: Not a bad place to watch the northern lights (sadly, not seen, and thus not pictured); it’s nearly totally dark out here

reviews.name: Town of Fort Smith
reviews.location: 174 McDougal Rd, Fort Smith, NT X0E 0A4, Canada
reviews.text: I spent a day in Fort Smith and had a really good time there! It’s a lovely little town nestled up at the eastern NWT/Alberta border. Visit Anna’s Restaurant, and get a coffee at Javapunks while you’re there

reviews.name: Kaeser's Stores Ltd
reviews.location: 76-80 Breynat St, Fort Smith, NT X0E 0A4, Canada
reviews.text: A very well-stocked supermarket for the remoteness of the city. I really appreciated that they carried Sap drinks

reviews.name: Fort Smith Fire Dept
reviews.location: 70 Breynat St, Fort Smith, NT X0E 0A4, Canada
reviews.text: The temperature clocks in front of the Fire Dept display the power of the (sub-)Arctic sun. In March, as the sun is staying up for longer, the clock faces will span 20°C depending on how long they’ve been baking in the sun.

reviews.name: Fort Smith Visitor Centre
reviews.location: 149 McDougal Rd, Fort Smith, NT X0E 0A4, Canada
reviews.text: The Visitor Centre was closed when I visited in March, and they appeared to be doing some reservations. I hope it’s nice when it reopens

reviews.name: Wood Buffalo Inn
reviews.text: Only stayed here for a single night, but the accommodations were great. The Inn is structured as a motel, but the rooms are stocked like entire apartments. If I come back to Fort Smith, I’ll definitely stay here again.

reviews.name: Javapunks (Cafe)
reviews.location: 101 King St, Fort Smith, NT X0E 0A4, Canada
reviews.text: Every town in the Northwest Territories has their cool coffee shop, and Javapunks is Fort Smith’s. They’ve got a decent drink coffee in a hip and cozy location. If I come back, I’d love to stay and do some work from here.

reviews.name: NSIXTY Trading Company Ltd.
reviews.location: 101 King St, Fort Smith, NT X0E 0A4, Canada
reviews.text: N60 Trading Company is a really interesting, well stocked hobby store. It’s such a gem for this kind of store to exist in such a remote location. I’m glad the people of the far north can get supplies for their hobbies, and games for the long and dark winters.

reviews.name: Northern Life Museum & Cultural Centre and Gift Shop
reviews.location: 110 King St, Fort Smith, NT X0E 0A4, Canada
reviews.text: I’m sad that I didn’t get to go into the Northern Life Museum, despite them claiming to be open. I even called them to no avail, a real shame

reviews.name: Anna's Restaurant
reviews.location: 338 Calder Ave, Fort Smith, NT X0E 0A4, Canada
reviews.text: Anna’s Restaurant was the only place that I ate while I was in Fort Smith, because after stopping in for brunch, I simply had to return for dinner to try the pizza (I got a calzone). Everything I had here was simply delicious, especially the incredible bread, and the towns were an absolute delight to talk to.

reviews.name: Woodcutter's Monument
reviews.text: Absolutely nothing to see in March, and a bit annoying to get to. Skip this one outside of summer

reviews.name: Mountain Portage
reviews.location: Unnamed Road, Wood Buffalo, AB T0P, Canada
reviews.text: A bit harrowing to reach in winter, you’ll need to walk from the Portage Parking, marked on the map, with skis or snowmobiles also being options. The views truly aren’t the best, but hey, it’s something to see

reviews.name: Mountain Portage Parking
reviews.text: At least in winter, this is really as far as you’re going to want to drive. As a bonus for stopping here, you can get a bit of a view of the frozen water below. …

reviews.name: Welcome to Fort Smith Sign
reviews.location: McDougal Rd, Fort Smith, NT X0E 0A4, Canada
reviews.text: A fine looking sign, for sure. People in town recommend coming out here, or to the airport, to get good pictures of the northern lights

reviews.name: Tim Hortons
reviews.location: 50 Trout St, Fort Smith, NT X0E 0A4, Canada
reviews.text: Definitely the most remote Tim Hortons that I’ve visited. And on account of that remoteness, the selection is a bit more limited here than at some of the locations down south. If you show up in the mornings, there’s something of a line, but it moves fast.

reviews.name: Little Buffalo River Falls Territorial Park
reviews.location: Fort Smith, Unorganized, NT X0E 0P0, Canada
reviews.text: There are so few places between Hay River and Fort Smith, and even fewer which are open in the winter. Little Buffalo River Falls were open and generally accessible, though not the most impressive. Still worth stopping (but keep that engine running).

reviews.name: Wood Buffalo National Park of Canada
reviews.text: A wonderful place to go for a drive. But know, it’s very very sparse, with quite few people traversing the roads. During winter, play it safe and don’t stray too far off the main roads

reviews.name: Big Buffalo River
reviews.location: Fort Smith, Unorganized, NT X0E 0R7, Canada
reviews.text: Big must be relative, and not to the region

reviews.name: Pine Point Bridge
reviews.location: Fort Smith, Unorganized, NT X0E 0R7, Canada
reviews.text: In a land of sparseness, everything is notable, and this bridge was lovely, vibrant hue of green, and gave some interesting views during wintertime

reviews.name: Esso
reviews.location: 921 MacKenzie Hwy Ss 22, Hay River, NT X0E 1G1, Canada
reviews.text: A full service gas station with some decently reasonable prices. Because it’s located on the main road, it’s easy to stop here just before leaving town

reviews.name: Georginas Place Thrift Shop
reviews.location: 69 Woodland Dr, Hay River, NT X0E 1G1, Canada
reviews.text: A small, well stocked thrift shop located in what feels like a house

reviews.name: Hay River Tourist Information
reviews.location: McBryan Dr, Hay River, NT X0E 0R3, Canada
reviews.text: While the center was shut when I came by in late March, they did have some of the finest art in the region on display just outside, and that was plenty for me

reviews.name: Rat Lake
reviews.location: Rat Lake, MacKenzie County, AB T0H 2P0, Canada
reviews.text: Completely inaccessible from Indian Cabins, sadly

reviews.name: Indian Cabins Trading Post
reviews.location: Hwy 35, Meander River, AB T0H 2P0, Canada
reviews.text: As you head south from the 60th Parallel by Hay River, Indian Cabins Trading Post is the first thing that you’ll hit south of the border. And what a wonderful place to stop, if only for Screw Stewie, a dog that’s all too excited to meet you

reviews.name: Welcome to the Northwest Territories Sign
reviews.location: AB-35, Meander River, AB T0H 2P0, Canada
reviews.text: In terms of border signs, this one is quite impressive, especially when compared to its contemporaries - the Welcome to Alberta sign opposite it and the signs by Fort Smith. The whole place is a ghost town if you make the journey in winter, with the exception of the odd car flying by

reviews.name: Welcome to Mackenzie County Sign
reviews.location: AB-35, Meander River, AB T0H 2P0, Canada
reviews.text: Much better than the Alberta sign a hundred meters in front of it. You got a sun and everything on the sign, it’s doing its own thing

reviews.name: Welcome to Alberta Sign
reviews.location: AB-35, Meander River, AB T0H 2P0, Canada
reviews.text: Albertans, let’s be honest. This sign isn’t bringing your province the glory that it deserves. You gotta dream bigger, especially when the NWT sign opposite yours is so much bigger and nicer

reviews.name: Sixtieth Parallel Territorial Park
reviews.location: Mackenzie Hwy, Fort Smith, Unorganized, NT X0E 0R1, Canada
reviews.text: If you’re looking to see the inside of any of the buildings, I’d recommend visiting in the summer months

reviews.name: Sixtieth Parallel Territorial Park Visitor Centre
reviews.location: Hwy 1, South Slave Region, NT X0E 0R1, Canada
reviews.text: Rating this on aesthetics alone, as the whole place was shut for winter when I visited in late March. With pristine, untouched snow, and tall ordinary trees surrounding the simple structure, the aesthetic was fine

reviews.name: Alexandra Falls Observation Deck
reviews.location: 1 Rte Waterfalls, Enterprise, NT X0E 1G3, Canada
reviews.text: This deck is situated out on the cliff face, above the falls, giving a sweeping view of Alexandra Falls and the lower river basin

reviews.name: Alexandra Falls
reviews.location: 1 Rte Waterfalls, Enterprise, NT X0E 1G3, Canada
reviews.text: Completely frozen in the winter, the Alexandra Falls make for a memorable visit regardless of the time of the year

reviews.name: Alexandra Falls Territorial Park Day Use Area
reviews.location: Rte Waterfalls, Enterprise, NT X0E 0R1, Canada
reviews.text: One of the few stops along the NWT Highways which was actually open and accessible during the winter. The trail was mostly packed snow leading to the observation pavilion.

reviews.name: Big Lake
reviews.location: 2-4 Courtoreille St, Hay River, NT X0E 1G2, Canada
reviews.text: Big Lake is the only real coffee shop in Hay River, and they make a decent cup of coffee and muffin. They also have more full meals, and for more meals than breakfast, but I never tried either; maybe my loss.

reviews.name: Hay River Public Beach
reviews.text: I came here to watch a sunrise in March, and it was -39°, the coldest temperature that I felt in the subarctic. It’s a nice place to take in the rising winter sun, but it can get seriously cold here, being exposed to the lake air.

reviews.name: Welcome to Enterprise Sign
reviews.text: Simple sign, could be a bit more fantabulous

reviews.name: Hay River Inukshuk
reviews.location: 73 Woodland Dr, Hay River, NT X0E 1G2, Canada
reviews.text: The Inukshuk is stood in front of the Fire Department, between the Canadian and Northwestern Territories flags, looking imposing as you drive into downtown Hay River. Quite a sight to behold

reviews.name: Hay River Fire Department
reviews.location: 73 Woodland Dr, Hay River, NT X0E 1G2, Canada
reviews.text: One of the more beautiful structures in Hay River, especially at dusk

reviews.name: Northmart
reviews.location: 81 Woodland Dr, Hay River, NT X0E 0R3, Canada
reviews.text: A very large store, in the historic and general sense, which has whatever you need. My main complaint is how early they close (6pm) as there were multiple times when I wanted a late night snack to no avail

reviews.name: Doghouse pub
reviews.location: 10 J Gagnier Rd, Hay River, NT X0E 1G1, Canada
reviews.text: I visited the Keys Lounge a few times before I decided to try the Doghouse Pub (they share a menu, including the bar options), and wow, as a solo diner I had a much better time eating at the bar. If you’re planning to eat alone, go in the back entrance and eat in The Doghouse at the bar.

reviews.name: Keys Dining Lounge & Restaurant
reviews.location: 10 J Gagnier Rd, Hay River, NT X0E 1G1, Canada
reviews.text: Keys Dining Lounge is located within the Ptarmigan Inn, and is most likely the nicest restaurant within 3hrs of Hay River. I came here a few times and really enjoyed the Poutine, Ribs, Wings, and the Burger (which also supports charity). …

reviews.name: Ptarmigan Inn
reviews.location: 10 J Gagnier Rd, Hay River, NT X0E 1G1, Canada
reviews.text: Whether you’re staying at the Ptarmigan Inn or not, they have one of the best restaurants in town (Keys Lounge) and one of the best bars in the surrounding 6hrs (Doghouse Pub). It’s a nice place to stop while you’re in town

reviews.name: Riverview Cineplex
reviews.location: 25 Studney Dr, Enterprise, NT X0E 0R1, Canada
reviews.text: With Yellowknife’s movie theatre now being shut, this may be the last cinema in the NWT. Sadly I couldn’t support them, I hope they survive and keep fighting the good fight

reviews.name: Ring's Pharmacy Ltd
reviews.location: 6 Courtoreille St, Hay River, NT X0E 0A9, Canada
reviews.text: A fairly full pharmacy and convenience store for the remoteness of the region

reviews.name: Town of Hay River
reviews.location: 62 Woodland Dr #100, Hay River, NT X0E 1G1, Canada
reviews.text: While it doesn’t necessarily have the best reputation among locals across the NWT, I enjoyed my days in Hay River. There’s a few hotels, a couple good restaurants, a coffee shop, and everything else you need to survive up here. Hay River is a fine place to visit

reviews.name: Cambridge Executive Suites
reviews.location: 31 Capital Dr #101, Hay River, NT X0E 1G1, Canada
reviews.text: I really did enjoy staying at the Cambridge Executive Suites, and like the people that own it, but when they only clean with a broom and dustpan, they leave a lot of hair in the rooms. Otherwise, the apartments are wonderful, but they need to invest in a vacuum

reviews.name: Town welcome sign
reviews.location: Q5VJ+8C, Hay River, NT X0E 1G5, Canada
reviews.text: Hey, it is a beautiful sign. You wanna stop and take it in on the way into town.

reviews.name: Junction of Highways 1 and 2
reviews.text: You’d think that there’d be more here, but in winter, this area was exceptionally dead except for the trucks passing by. Whether you’re going to/from Fort Smith, Hay River, or Yellowknife, you’ll be passing through Enterprise which is entirely comprised by this intersection.

reviews.name: Information Board
reviews.location: Fort Smith, Unorganized, NT X0E 0L0, Canada
reviews.text: This information board is located at the intersection of Route 1 and Route 3, as 3 dead-ends into 1. It’s a fine board, I guess it’s something to note

reviews.name: Deh Cho Bridge
reviews.location: South Slave Region, NT X0E 0L0, Canada
reviews.text: The Northwest Territories is so sparse of human creations that any are notable. Arguably, the Deh Cho Bridge is the most spectacular landmark outside of the few cities of the NWT, with a stark prominence visible from miles away on either …

reviews.name: Big River Service Centre LP
reviews.location: 1 NT-3 Lot 3, Fort Providence, NT X0E 0L0, Canada
reviews.text: One of the better places to stop on the route connecting Hay River and Yellowknife, with reasonably priced gas and some hot food, snacks, and drinks. If you’ve got the time, stop off in Fort Providence

reviews.name: Snowshoe Inn Cafe & Craft Shop
reviews.location: Mackenzie Drive, Fort Providence, NT X0E 0A7, Canada
reviews.text: A must stop location if you’re driving from Hay River to Yellowknife or visa-versa. Great options for either breakfast or lunch, and some nice coffee with two brews to choose from. They also have a little shop next door with arts and crafts that they’ll open if you ask

reviews.name: North Arm Territorial Park Day Use Area
reviews.text: In the winter, the lake is entirely frozen over, so you’ll see a person or two camping in a car in the parking lot, and the lake is otherwise untouched. It’s a beautiful sight to be seen and it nearly looks like the moon or mars

reviews.name: Frank Channel Bridge
reviews.text: In a land nearly untouched by man, a single and simple bridge becomes all too notable. The Frank Channel Bridge was under construction when I passed across it in March, and there was a street light enforcing the single lane of traffic.

reviews.name: Miss Saigon
reviews.location: Inside Kim’s Confectionary, 5309 Franklin Ave, Yellowknife, NT X1A 1E3, Canada
reviews.text: Miss Saigon is an absolutely delicious takeout option just a few blocks outside of downtown Yellowknife. Located inside of Kim’s Confectionery, this unassuming location doesn’t have the best aesthetics, but makes some delicious Vietnamese food with great portions for a low cost

reviews.name: Kim's Confectionary
reviews.location: 5309 Franklin Ave, Yellowknife, NT X1A 2P1, Canada
reviews.text: A slightly smaller convenience store, but they carry a variety of more snacky options, and a few more packaged staples. Miss Saigon’s is located inside of Kim’s, and is great!

reviews.name: Dettah Ice Road
reviews.location: School Draw Ave, Yellowknife, NT X1A 3G2, Canada
reviews.text: It’s less of a singular road (at the Yellowknife portion) and more of a, people drive on the lake to go where they need to. Multiple entrances and multiple exits, but with one major artery heading further into the lake.

reviews.name: Snowkings' Winter Festival
reviews.location: 1 Kingsway, Yellowknife Bay, Yellowknife, NT X1A 2P2, Canada
reviews.text: This year was the 31st anniversary of Snowkings’ Winter Festival, in which they build an expansive ice castle on the frozen lake, with an ice carving contest situated outside. It’s a truly impressive endeavor, executed to an excellent …

reviews.name: Gallery of the Midnight Sun
reviews.location: 5005 Bryson Dr, Yellowknife, NT X1A 2A3, Canada
reviews.text: A gallery with a variety of local crafts and taxidermies, including a number of beautiful, more premium art pieces. It’s nice to walk through this gallery regardless of whether you intend to buy anything.

reviews.name: Down to Earth Gallery
reviews.location: 5007 Bryson Dr, Yellowknife, NT X1A 2A3, Canada
reviews.text: A lovely little gallery and local craft and art shop, which is packed full of goodies. The location is located inside of a log cabin ordained with local art

reviews.name: NWT Brewing Company / The Woodyard Brewhouse & Eatery
reviews.location: 3905 Franklin Ave, Yellowknife, NT X1A 2S6, Canada
reviews.text: If you have some spare time in Yellowknife, plop yourself down at the bar at NWT Brewing and you’ll discover a number of great local beers, and equally great local people. They brew a beer each year for the Snowkings Ice Festival, on the lake next door, each winter.

reviews.name: Aurora Emporium Art Gallery
reviews.location: 4701 Franklin Ave, Yellowknife, NT X1A 2P1, Canada
reviews.text: The owner is a longtime Yellowknifer who sells a number of local crafts, perfect for gifts down south. They’ll also print your pictures on mugs, especially ones of northern lights.

reviews.name: Centre Square Mall
reviews.text: One of the most prominent buildings in downtown Yellowknife, and while it may not be as thriving as it once was, evidenced by a lot of people standing around and a whole section being closed off. Still, they have a Tim Hortons, a nice Visitor Centre with mementos for tourists, and a decent library. If you’re in YK, stop by

reviews.name: Barren Ground Coffee
reviews.text: Really delicious coffee, roasted locally in the NWT. Love supporting a local business, especially when the drip coffee is so good.

reviews.name: Houcine's Your Independent Grocer Yellowknife 50th Ave
reviews.location: 4802 Franklin Ave #14, Yellowknife, NT X1A 1C4, Canada
reviews.text: A very full supermarket, with slightly higher prices, though nothing unreasonable considering the remoteness of the location. If you’re visiting Yellowknife from another country, there’s a few Canadian touristic products for you to buy as gift or souvenirs

reviews.name: YK Centre Clock
reviews.text: If you give me a clock, I’m going to need to take a picture with the high score, or rather the low score in this case. It was -32° here, but -39° on the trip (Hay River Beach at sunrise)

reviews.name: United Nations Tank Display
reviews.text: You seriously don’t expect to see a UN Tank in Canada, but this one appears to have been abandoned here, and was fully covered in snow when I visited

reviews.name: Legislative Assembly of the Northwest Territories
reviews.location: 4570 48 St, Yellowknife, NT NT X1A 3A5, Canada
reviews.text: One of the more impressive city hall buildings that I’ve ever seen in my travels, as there’s a giant polar bear skin laying on the floor intimidatingly, and a huge Zinc wall behind the main dais

reviews.name: North of 60° Mining Memorial
reviews.text: A fairly simple monument, but an elegant looking one at that. May they rest in Peace, indeed

reviews.name: Museum Restaurant by Sundog
reviews.text: I visited the Heritage Centre first thing in the morning, before I’d eaten breakfast, and so I stopped at Sundog more out of convenience than intention. Regardless, I really enjoyed the breakfast sandwich and potatoes that I had here.

reviews.name: Prince of Wales Northern Heritage Centre
reviews.text: One of my favorite attractions in Yellowknife, and the larger NWT, this museum both tells the history of the region and the historical people, and displays a lot of art and culture of the locals that call this far northern region home. …

reviews.name: Ceremonial Circle
reviews.text: An attraction, of sorts. There’s a pathway of all the regional flags connecting City Hall from the Heritage Center and Legislative Assembly, along the body of water

reviews.name: United in Celebration sculpture
reviews.location: Sombe K'e Civic Plaza, 4910 52 St, Yellowknife, NT X0E, Canada
reviews.text: This sculpture depicts two people dancing in shadow with shields (?) in their hands, and is situated right at the water’s edge, though in winter it’s a bit hard to tell.

reviews.name: Somba K'e Civic Plaza
reviews.text: In wintertime, there’s not a ton here, but for a large tree and the United in Celebration sculpture, and a ton of wind and cold

reviews.name: Yellowknife City Hall
reviews.text: While the building was closed when I visited (on a Sunday morning), I did enjoy exploring the surrounding area and its sparse art. If you’re hoping to use the building to warm up, plan to go elsewhere

reviews.name: Javaroma Gourmet Coffee & Tea
reviews.location: 5201 Franklin Ave, Yellowknife, NT X1A 3S9, Canada
reviews.text: Javaroma is the (only) Yellowknife local chain, with a few locations scattered around the northern capital city. The coffee isn’t incredible, as is typical with most chains, but I really appreciate that they opened early on the weekends. They also had some fancy looking pastries

reviews.name: Budget Car & Truck Rental
reviews.location: 20 Airport Road, Yellowknife, NT X1A 3T2, Canada
reviews.text: Don’t be afraid of the slightly scary sign posted outside of the closed airport location, someone most likely is on the way to meet you at your reservation time. …

reviews.name: Yellowknife Airport
reviews.location: 100 Idaa Rd, Yellowknife, NT NT X1A 3T2, Canada
reviews.text: In terms of tiny airports in remote places of the globe, Yellowknife Airport is decently well equipped and serviced! I also believe that this is the only airport with a life sized polar bear in the main terminal, but I’ll have to keep …

reviews.name: Tim Hortons
reviews.location: Pearson International Airport - T1 Domestic Post Security - Near, Gate D42, Mississauga, ON L5P 1B2, Canada
reviews.text: This Tim Hortons had a decent selection at 8pm, with nearly all of the donut bins remaining full. Just what I needed on a quick stopover

reviews.name: Plaza Premium Lounge Toronto Pearson (US Transborder, Terminal 1)
reviews.location: Toronto Pearson Int'l Airport, Gate E77, International Departures, Terminal 1, Mississauga, ON L4V 1R9, Canada
reviews.text: There’s two Plaza Premium Lounges in the Toronto Airport, and they both take Priority Pass. Neither is very good, and this is the worse of the two. The food really isn’t great, and it’s often quite crowded where you’re waiting for a while …

reviews.name: Plaza Premium Lounge Toronto Pearson (Domestic Departures, Terminal 1)
reviews.location: Toronto Pearson International Airport, Right After Security, Domestic Departures, Level 3, 6301 Silver Dart Dr Terminal 1 Departures, Mississauga, ON L5P 1B2, Canada
reviews.text: There’s two Plaza Premium Lounges in the Toronto Airport. They book take Priority Pass, and neither is really very good, but this is the better of the two. The food isn’t great, nor is the drink selection. Make sure not to lose your ticket, and they circulate and check tickets to make sure that no one overstays their visit.

reviews.name: Toronto Pearson Int'l Airport
reviews.location: 6301 Silver Dart Dr, Mississauga, ON L5P 1B2, Canada
reviews.text: The Toronto Airport will be your launchpad if you’re flying from the eastern side of the United States, and are trying to go to northern Canada, as this was the easiest way for me to get to Yellowknife. …

reviews.name: ARCO
reviews.text: By far the cheapest gas around Haight/Divisidaro area, and they have working mobile payment readers on the pumps. …

reviews.name: Dunkin'
reviews.location: 30th & Market St Station Amtrak Food Court, Philadelphia, PA 19104
reviews.text: This is the Dunkin’ in the main hall, and there’s actually a second, less crowded one, near the SEPTA Regional Rails. America Runs on Dunkin’ especially when it’s the only option in the train hall (but for a Pret down the hall).

reviews.name: Chase Sapphire Lounge by The Club New York City LGA
reviews.location: LaGuardia Airport, Terminal B, Level 1A, East Elmhurst, NY 11371
reviews.text: The Chase Sapphire Lounge is a Priority Pass app (at least for people who have it through a Chase credit card), and operates by a QR code and website system for food ordering, but there’s also smaller dishes available at counters around the room, a full bar, and a smattering of drink fridges and snack jars.

reviews.name: Chickie's & Pete's Terminal A
reviews.text: Airport Terminal location of a classic Philly area restaurant known for their Crab Fries. They have nearly their whole menu here, with a decent beer selection. I appreciated that they had a quick togo option as well

reviews.name: Ashley's Restaurant and Bar
reviews.text: Ashley’s is a neighborhood bar and restaurant with an extensive salad bar and good pasta and burgers. I’ve been here a few times, and everything that I’ve ordered has been pretty consistently solid.

reviews.name: AMC DINE-IN Painters Crossing 9
reviews.text: One of the dine-in AMC Theatres, which will still sell you popcorn, pretzels, and the classic movie snacks and drinks, but they also have a fuller food and drink menu which they’ll deliver to your seat. …

reviews.name: Target
reviews.location: 500 N Congress Ave, Lake Park, FL 33403
reviews.text: Got there right after they opened and the place went quite empty and quiet. No issues to report, it’s a big store

reviews.name: Delco's Original Steaks & Hoagies
reviews.text: My local home cheesesteak spot, they’ve got a good sandwich, with some Amoroso-style bread. Their medium is huge, I can barely finish it when I’m famished. A large would feel a small family, I would assume.

reviews.name: Bread and Butter Kitchen
reviews.text: A decent and slightly more reasonably priced lunch option, potentially on account of it being a peninsula away from downtown Annapolis. The omelettes were decent, though nothing was too memorable

reviews.name: Love & Honey Fried Chicken
reviews.text: Really tasty chicken tenders, and a great portion for the cost. They drizzle honey atop, which is just such a great topper

reviews.name: WhatSub Sub Shop Palm Beach Gardens
reviews.location: 10800 N Military Trl #120, Palm Beach Gardens, FL 33410
reviews.text: WhatSub has a selection of Cold and Hot Sandwiches which all seemed to really be quite sizable. I ordered the Chicken Parm, and it had a ton of Chicken on it, served on some great bread

reviews.name: Oceana Coffee Drive Thru
reviews.text: Oceana has some decent drip coffee for a fair price. While they have a fairly well sized interior, they also have a drive through as well

reviews.name: Lingonberry (Northlake)
reviews.location: 4258 Northlake Blvd, Palm Beach Gardens, FL 33410
reviews.text: Really solid drip coffee for a reasonable price

reviews.name: Sancho Pistola's
reviews.text: Burritos aren’t huge, and are a bit on the pricier side for the area, but they are very tasty.

reviews.name: Impresso Express
reviews.text: The drip coffee is ok!

reviews.name: JD Vance Mural
reviews.text: It’s hideous, it’s perfect. I love it, the eyes followed me my whole walk home, and may still be following me now

reviews.name: Front Street Walls
reviews.text: Beautiful, story-tall murals lining Front Street, under the El

reviews.name: Mecha Noodle Bar
reviews.text: Mecha makes a decent pho, in a trendy and aesthetically pleasing bar / restaurant space. The Happy Hour specials look decent as well

reviews.name: AMC Broadstreet 7
reviews.text: Certainly on the smaller end for urban AMCs, Broadstreet has a single concession counter, and all of the theatres are all located along a long hallway. That being said, it’s a perfectly lovely place to watch movies.

reviews.name: Sumalee Thai
reviews.text: I ordered Chicken Pad Thai delivery from here, and it was extremely meh.

reviews.name: Loco Pez
reviews.text: Loco Pez makes a pretty good burrito, which made for a really sizable lunch

reviews.name: Rowhome Coffee - Front Street
reviews.text: Rowhome Coffee makes their Breakfast Sandwiches on Pretzels! How ingenious! The Sausage, Egg, and Cheese ones were delicious and served piping hot. The coffee was fine

reviews.name: Gilda
reviews.text: Gilda is a small coffee shop and bakery, but wow do they pack a mighty punch. You can get a drip coffee to stay, and they’ll give you refills, and the pastries are simply out-of-this-world. I’ll have to come back and try the rest of the menu.

reviews.name: ReAnimator Coffee
reviews.text: ReAnimator’s a neighborhood coffee spot, but with its central location, it really serves as the hub/heart of the local neighborhood. I like their drip coffee

reviews.name: PrimoHoagies
reviews.text: PrimoHoagies are a great option for a quick and convenient lunch. You can order ahead on their website, and then go pick it up when it’s done, typically in 10mins. I really like their Italian Hoagie.

reviews.name: Caletta
reviews.text: Caletta is the bar area of Bastia / Hotel Anna and Bel, and it’s an intimate, lovely spot to stop for a more elevated drink and snack inside of the fancy hotel. …

reviews.name: Philly Halal Gyro
reviews.text: An extremely reasonably priced food truck, serving Halal Food. I liked the Chicken Over Rice, but it was a bit heavy on the hot sauce. I’ll go a bit lighter next time, and may try another meat.

reviews.name: The Richmond Shops IGA
reviews.text: A neighborhood grocer with a decent selection of fresh produce, meat, and baked goods. They got all of the national brands, as well as a number of store brands, across products

reviews.name: Manhasset
reviews.text: This LIRR station has a nice indoor portion which provides places to sit down, and to provide some shelter from the elements

reviews.name: Tom Seaver Statue
reviews.text: The statue is situated directly in front of the main facade of the stadium, so it’s easy to frame it in your best shots of the complex

reviews.name: Sammy's Woodfired Pizza
reviews.location: Terminal 4, 1 World Wy, Los Angeles, CA 90045
reviews.text: I came here for breakfast, and ordered the breakfast sandwich with potatoes, and while it was very pricey, it was all delicious and exactly what my body needed.

reviews.name: AmericanAirlinesFlagshipLounge
reviews.text: A very nice First Class lounge, don’t get me wrong, but the food was all very fancy, and not at all what I wanted after flying for 15hrs, so I brought in food from downstairs, which they were totally fine with.

reviews.name: Qantas International First Lounge Los Angeles
reviews.text: This lounge functions more as a sit down restaurant, where you may need to wait for a table. Not the best snacks outside of the dining area

reviews.name: Chelsea Lounge JFK - British Airways & American
reviews.location: JFK Terminal 8, Central Terminal Area, JFK International Airport, NY 11430
reviews.text: The Chelsea Lounge in JFK is the First Class lounge that services American and British Airways passengers. These lounges are uber luxurious, and have a menu full of delicacies. While they didn’t have the Steak Frites, I didn’t so enjoy the Tartare and Pappardelle before my cross country flight.

reviews.name: Pennsylvania Railroad World War II Memorial
reviews.location: William H. Gray III 30th Street Station, 2955 Market St, Philadelphia, PA 19104
reviews.text: The signature artwork of 30th St: a humongous statue of an angel holding a fallen man on a pedestal, lined with the names of the fallen.

reviews.name: Amtrak Philadelphia Train Station
reviews.text: 30th St Station serves both Amtrak and SEPTA, and thus serves as Southeastern PA’s main connector to the region and to the whole Mid-Atlantic area. …

reviews.name: MOD Pizza
reviews.text: A good place to get a fairly quick and decently cheap, fully customizable pizza. It’s the kind of pie that doesn’t age the best, so eat it quickly

reviews.name: Margaret Kuo's Kitchen
reviews.location: 1109 W Baltimore Pike Suite A, Media, PA 19063
reviews.text: Margaret Kuo has long been a quality restaurant chain in the Philly area, and I was happy to find that was still true in the 2020s. Had a great dinner at the Granite Run location, with a variety of Chinese and Pan-Asian dishes. Love that they bring out peanuts and cucumbers as free appetizers.

reviews.name: Meghan's
reviews.text: Meghan’s is a staple of Concord Township, as its beloved greasy spoon diner. While they’re often full, it never takes too long for a table to open up. …

reviews.name: Dock Bridge
reviews.location: Passaic River, Harrison NJ, Harrison, NJ 07029
reviews.text: The Dock Bridge is the railway bridge which crosses the Passaic River. It’s pretty rusted over, and something of an eyesore, but it’s got its charm

reviews.name: Sheetz
reviews.text: Now I’m a Wawa guy, so I’m coming in here with a slant, but the main problem with Sheetz is the speed. When you have a basic order, like a simple breakfast sandwich, you want them ready to go. At Sheetz they actually brag about the fact that they making things to order, which is obscenely slow at most locations, including this one.

reviews.name: The Pied Piper of Bedford County
reviews.text: I wasn’t expecting this funny little guy, when I was driving east across Pennsylvania, but life exists to delight, I suppose. What is his story, where is he from, what secrets does he keep?

reviews.name: Lookout Point Mt. Ararat
reviews.text: If you stop at the Flight 93 Memorial on the way from Pittsburgh back east, you’ll be driving across Mt. Ararat. You owe it to yourself to stop and take in the vista for a moment.

reviews.name: Scenic Overlook
reviews.text: It’s quite the vista, Mt. Ararat. It almost makes me feel like I’m back in the hills of Napa county

reviews.name: Post-9/11 U.S. Armed Forces Memorial at Patriot Park
reviews.text: This is an accompanying Memorial, across the street from the official Flight 93 Memorial, this one with flags and the shadow of a person kneeling at a soldier’s memorial. There were only a few flags laid out, far fewer than I was anticipating.

reviews.name: Memorial Plaza
reviews.text: The Memorial Plaza is located at the end of a long walkway from the Visitor Shelter, and consists of a large wavy cement wall with the names of the deceased on it. It’s really a touching tribute, where the walk gives you time to reflect.

reviews.name: Flight 93 National Memorial - Visitor Center
reviews.text: The Flight 93 Visitor Center itself is perched up on a hill overlooking the disaster’s field, which is now the Memorial Plaza today. The building itself is truly a piece of art, made of simple concrete and glass walls. Unfortunately the architecture functions like something of a wind tunnel so it can get very cold inside.

reviews.name: Flight 93 National Memorial
reviews.text:
A touching memorial to the Flight 93 tragedy that occurred on September 11th. There are multiple buildings that encompass the memorial, in some
ways recognizing the field that was scattered here. There’s also a giant wind chime on the way in, in a stunning tower.

reviews.name: YINZ Coffee Friendship
reviews.text: Decent coffee, great best, incredible name

reviews.name: Shibam Coffee
reviews.text: Very cool aesthetics, and interesting sounding drinks, but I really didn’t enjoy what I got.

reviews.name: Pamela's | P&G Diner
reviews.text: Pamela’s is a Pittsburgh institution, and their hotcakes are renowned. They’re like crepes, almost, and you can get them filled with fruit and cream. I always get The Morning After breakfast special, and substitute in Specialty Hot Cakes …

reviews.name: Morrow Park
reviews.text: Less a park, and more a statue with some grass, Morrow Park isn’t much to write home about, not to denigrate the perfectly fine statue at its heart.

reviews.name: FET-FISK restaurant + bar
reviews.text: Didn’t have a reservation and queued up with a party of 5 about 10 minutes before they opened and got seated at the bar. Fet-Fisk is a very cool upscale restaurant with a variety of excellent seafood and meat options. I had the Tartar, the …

reviews.name: Phipps Conservatory and Botanical Gardens
reviews.text: Phipps Conservatory is an outstandingly beautiful building, filled with a variety of plants from around the world. However, the most notable thing about this museum isn’t alive, and is entirely Silicon-based. The glass structure of the …

reviews.name: Flag Monument
reviews.text: A very simple monument, with a large, gravestone-esque rock and a lone flag on a flagpole. The monument recognizes America on its 150th birthday, and now at year 250, it’s been here for a century.

reviews.name: Scotty Dog Statue
reviews.location: University Center, 5032 Forbes Ave, Pittsburgh, PA 15213
reviews.text: This statue is new (since I graduated), and I’m not certain how I feel about it. It’s a fine statue, sure, but does it belong in front of the UC? Put it in front of the admissions building

reviews.name: Flagstaff Hill
reviews.text: Flagstaff Hill is the far north portion of Schenley Park, which connects Phipps Conservatory with Carnegie Mellon’s campus. It’s a lovely place to sit, and a convenient place to cut across to get to Oakland.

reviews.name: Newell-Simon Hall
reviews.text: Newell-Simon Hall is one of the Robots centers on campus, and the building is dressed accordingly. For the last fifteen (plus) years, Tank the Robo-Receptionist has greeted you, and there’s occasionally robotics displays on the first floor. …

reviews.name: The Mall
reviews.text: There are two interconnected green lawns on Carnegie Mellon’s main campus: The Cut, extending to Forbes, and The Mall, with its iconic shot extended out to Pitt’s Cathedral of Learning.

reviews.name: The Fence
reviews.text: The most iconic landmark on Carnegie Mellon’s campus. The Fence has strict rules, it can only be painted by hand and by brush (no rollers), and it can only be painted after midnight. To hold The Fence, you need to keep two (or more) people …

reviews.name: The Bride of Penn Ave
reviews.text: A hauntingly beautiful painting of the Penn Ave of Pittsburgh yester. Maybe we’ll get back there one day

reviews.name: Pittsburgh Glass Center
reviews.text: Pittsburgh Glass Center is a combination studio space and teaching studio, where you can take classes to learn the craft of glassblowing. The studio had an exhibit filled with the students’ art, and it was simply exceptional; with some …

reviews.name: Friendship Perk & Brew
reviews.text: Friendship Perk & Brew is local coffee shop and sit-down breakfast restaurant has a very homey feel, with some ok java and good pastries.

reviews.name: täkō
reviews.text:
A hip and modern taqueria offering a diversity of elevated tacos in a smaller dark multilevel bar
room. The eponymous Tako taco is their speciality, and while it’s very good, it’s not my favorite.

reviews.name: Gates Center for Computer Science
reviews.location: Gates Center for Computer Science, 5000 Forbes Ave, Pittsburgh, PA 15213
reviews.text: Built when the Foundation was still called the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, the building’s most notable feature is the Guggenheim-esque spiral staircase that oh so slowly snakes down the mainly vertical building.

reviews.name: The Cut
reviews.text: The Cut is the nickname for the central lawn that goes from Forbes Avenue to Hunt Library, including the Fence. I’ve always believed that it’s named that because you need to “cut” across it to get to the other half of the buildings

reviews.name: Walking to the Sky
reviews.text: Walking to the Sky is one of the more prominent artworks on Carnegie Mellon’s campus, maybe second only to The Fence. That being said, I, among many other alums (and I’m sure current day students), really don’t love it.

reviews.name: Google Pittsburgh
reviews.text: When you search “affordable living” on the internal search engine, it sends you to the Pittsburgh office’s page. …

reviews.name: Bakery Square
reviews.text: Bakery Square is a shopping and building complex with a few parking garages, gyms, restaurants and corporate offices. Many of the photos included are from Google Pittsburgh, which is located across two of the buildings here, and includes an employee (and their guest) exclusive cafe.

reviews.name: Steaks West Chester
reviews.location: 698 E Market St Unit 3, West Chester, PA 19382
reviews.text: These folks make a good cheesesteak, the bread was a bit different from what I was expecting, but not in a bad way

reviews.name: Golden Valley Coffee Roasters
reviews.location: 208 Carter Dr Suite 13B, West Chester, PA 19382
reviews.text: They’ve just got a small little store in their larger production building, but they’ve got their beans a-brewing (just a little bit of drip they offered for free), and a ton of varieties to choose from in-house. I’ll definitely be coming back

reviews.name: Ravanesi Pizzeria, Inc.
reviews.text: You need to make a reservation for Ravanesi two weeks in advance, and they ask you how many pizzas you plan to eat that far out. But it’s not hard to see why; they’ve got exceptional pizza dough, which is made into some equally fantastic …

reviews.name: Delaware Border State Sign
reviews.text: Difficult to imagine that Delaware has endless anything, much less discoveries.

reviews.name: Governor Ritchie Scenic Overlook
reviews.text: This is the first opportunity to stop as you’re leaving Annapolis, and while it may be too early for you to be needing a break, it’s a worthwhile stop as you get two attractions in one.

reviews.name: Gold Star Family Monument
reviews.text: While certainly the secondary monument on the hill, the Gold Star Families Memorial is almost the more visually impressive of the two. I love the shadow play of the sculpture.

reviews.name: Maryland World War II Memorial
reviews.text: This Memorial is an impressive visual, on a prominent hillside as you leave Annapolis to go north. The WWII Memorial is a somber site, comprised of an amphitheater of sorts, built up to a star and flags.

reviews.name: Liberty Bell Replica
reviews.text: Situated right at the entrance of St. John’s College, this Liberty Bell is a replica of the original bell before it was cracked, purportedly

reviews.name: Guardians of the First Amendment Memorial
reviews.text: Visiting this one in April 2026 felt especially prescient as we appear to be living through history. It’s funny how things repeat themselves, almost

reviews.name: Kunta Kinte - Alex Haley Memorial
reviews.text: While the statues themselves aren’t the most impressive, I did appreciate the creative arrangement, and the powerful placards scattered around the piers. The memorial is very centrally located in downtown Annapolis, stop for a moment and appreciate it

reviews.name: Mills Fine Wine and Spirits
reviews.text: Quite an expansive wine and spirits store with varietals from all over the world. I like the little maps of all the wine growing regions of each country’s section, and really appreciate that they carry wine and mead.

reviews.name: Reclaimed of Annapolis
reviews.text: An upper-end thrift shop for furniture, much of which has been fixed up since its inception

reviews.name: Annapolis Essentials
reviews.text: If you’re looking to pick up some Old Bay sweatpants on your trip to Maryland, Annapolis Essentials is the place for you. It’s all very touristy, you won’t find anything small and local here.

reviews.name: Back Creek Books
reviews.text: This store has quite the collection of rare and eclectic books. Though the store isn’t especially expansive, there were half a dozen cabinets each with a dozen unique books.

reviews.name: Colonial Annapolis Historic District
reviews.text: Colonial Annapolis is a historic cobblestone area, with a number of notable events in its distant history. Today it’s a lovely shopping area, albeit a bit touristy, with tons of Navy men and women around.

reviews.name: State House Cannon
reviews.text: The cannon looks a bit rough, but it’s had quite the storied history, immortalized with a plaque on it. The thing is mounted on the State House hill, point outwards.

reviews.name: The Annapolis Pottery
reviews.text: An Annapolis institution that I’ve been visiting for my whole life. Rooms upon rooms of every kind of pottery for every use that you can think of, and a few more. If you’re visiting Annapolis for a day trip, perusing this pottery is a must.

reviews.name: Baron Johann de Kalb
reviews.text: Located on the westside of the State House, de Kalb is standing shaking his fist to the sky. He really embodies the great energy of the capitol grounds.

reviews.name: Maryland State House
reviews.text: Annapolis is a town built around a hill by the water, with the State House perched atop the mound. That means that you can see this magnificent building from nearly the whole of Annapolis. In the spring the cherry blossoms really add to the aesthetic. There’s a few statues and a cannon on the grounds

reviews.name: William Preston Lane Jr. Memorial Bay Bridge
reviews.text: The Chesapeake Bay Bridge truly is an impressive bridge to traverse because of its length and various segments with their distinct regions. If you’re afraid of heights, looking around may give you a trippy sensation

reviews.name: Welcome to Maryland sign
reviews.text: It would be annoying to be the person that they left behind, but at least they made the rule afterwards

reviews.name: Buffalo Wild Wings
reviews.text: Large beers and decent wings with a large amount of TVs on every wall playing a variety of sports, what more could you ask for

reviews.name: Passing Through mural
reviews.text: An extremely difficult mural to capture from Amtrak, as you need to be sitting on the right side on a southbound train to/through Philadelphia

reviews.name: South Station
reviews.text: South Station is one of the major train stations in Boston, of which there are a few. The building itself is fairly unique looking though honestly I don’t love it. I wish they had more food options inside

reviews.name: Kendall/MIT
reviews.text: One of the quirkier T stops that I’ve visited, with a few attractions in the station itself. The Red line stops here

reviews.name: Point Park
reviews.text: The self-proclaimed Most Innovative Square Mile on the Planet, and why not. Who is honestly going to try to prove otherwise

reviews.name: Galaxy Park
reviews.text: A cute little triangular cement park with a globe of sorts in the middle of a fountain. The nicest thing about this very non-green park is the surrounds

reviews.name: The Liberty, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Boston
reviews.text: Stayed here for a work event, and the hotel itself was extremely beautiful, I heard it used to be a jail. My room was in the main building, which seemed to be unique among my coworkers, regardless I really enjoyed my room and my stay.

reviews.name: Viale
reviews.text: A lovely place for dinner that can accommodate large parties. I really enjoyed the oysters, the octopus, and the steak when I came here for a work event.

reviews.name: Google Cambridge
reviews.text: A lovely office comprised of three towers, connected across most floors in a very confusing manner. If you’re not a local, prepare to get lost at least once

reviews.name: CVS
reviews.text: A fine CVS. They had a decent enough selection, but locking up deodorant is beyond excessive

reviews.name: GetGo Gas Station
reviews.text: A fine enough gas station; the prices weren’t too egregious (all things considered)

reviews.name: Jenny Globe
reviews.text: There aren’t a ton of notable sights as you cross Pennsylvania on the Turnpike, but the Jenny Globe certainly is one of them.

reviews.name: CAVA
reviews.text: CAVA is a fast-casual chain which makes middle eastern style food for a reasonable price. I liked the Greek Salad, though the hummus (substituted for tzatziki) wasn’t incredible.

reviews.name: Masamoto Asian Grill & Sushi Bar
reviews.text: Masmoto is a higher end sushi restaurant with a broader array of Asian entrees. We tried a bit of everything, and it was all good! The Sashimi Platter was especially well plated, and all of the fish was extremely fresh. …

reviews.name: Booths Corner Collectibles
reviews.location: 1362 Naamans Creek Rd, Garnet Valley, PA 19060
reviews.text: I absolutely love this stand at Booths Corner, these are my go-to movie guys, and it seems like every week they’ve replenished their wares of movies. The best part is that you’re getting them for $1, an unheard of price in America today! You can’t even rent a movie for that low

reviews.name: Booths Corner Arcade
reviews.location: 1362 Naamans Creek Rd, Garnet Valley, PA 19060
reviews.text: There’s an arcade inside of the Booths Corner Farmer’s Market! It’s not incredibly large or fancy, but there’s a small room’s worth of games, including a few pinball games

reviews.name: The Club SFO
reviews.location: San Francisco International Airport, Harvey Milk Terminal 1, International Terminal Departures Level, San Francisco, CA 94128
reviews.text: There’s a Priority Pass lounge in Terminal 1 now! The Club does something close to a 1-in, 1-out system for entry, which makes sense as there’s a fixed amount of seating, and food and drink are app based which requires delivery to a …

reviews.name: San Franpsycho
reviews.location: San Francisco International Airport, HARVEY MILK TERMINAL 1, San Francisco, CA 94128
reviews.text: A local SF brand with fun apparel they make honoring the Bay Area, especially the city. You see them at a lot of neighborhoods’ farmers markets, and now in SFO

reviews.name: Wagon Wheel Barbeque
reviews.text: My rule with barbecue is typically that I don’t eat it unless I can see smoke coming out of the place, and while that wasn’t the case with Wagon Wheel, I did really enjoy all of the things I tried there

reviews.name: Google PLYM1625
reviews.text: There’s a ton of the recent Android OS figurines on the roof of this building (which is only accessible to employees and their guests). I really enjoyed taking a work call of the Android 13 swing.

reviews.name: Town Centre
reviews.text: A decent little shopping complex with a few restaurants, big box stores, and a bank or two.

reviews.name: Bronze Lyricist - By Bruce Hasson
reviews.location: 1842 N Shoreline Blvd, Mountain View, CA 94043
reviews.text: The statue isn’t too far back from the road, and is quite aesthetically pleasing. It’s unfortunately covered in some rusted bird poop stains

reviews.name: The Orb
reviews.location: 292 N Shoreline Blvd, Mountain View, CA 94043
reviews.text: I can appreciate an abstract piece of art. It’s fun to walk through it and look up at the various openings. At night, the structure is lit up with bright and changing colors

reviews.name: The Ameswell Hotel
reviews.text: My work held a happy hour / dinner event at The Ameswell Hotel, and it was great. The place has a good vibe, and the fire pits were a hot attraction as the sun set. The inside bar is very cool as well

reviews.name: Google Mountain View - Bay View
reviews.location: 100 Bay Vw Dr, Mountain View, CA 94043
reviews.text: One of the newer Googleplex campuses, with a bird’s nest looking building, large security gates, and an exotic interior filled with giant sculptures and newer amenities.

reviews.name: Google Bay View 4
reviews.location: 400 Bay Vw Dr GSuites, Mountain View, CA 94043
reviews.text: These are the Google dorm/hotels, which are only for employees. And while the location is extremely convenient for visiting Googlers going to the eastern portion of the MTV campus, I really didn’t love the rooms themselves

reviews.name: Wells Coffee Tarpon River
reviews.text: Wells Coffee has a delicious drip coffee

reviews.name: MAASS Restaurant at The Four Seasons
reviews.location: 525 N Fort Lauderdale Beach Blvd, Fort Lauderdale, FL 33304
reviews.text: MAASS has a Michelin star, and from the moment that you’re seated, you can clearly see why. I had a fantastic brunch here, and while everything was excellent, the pancake was really the standout of the meal. I’ve been thinking about that sweet stack of cakes for much of the last month.

reviews.name: Shell
reviews.text: If you’re headed back to PA, and you have ¾ of a tank or less, stop here and get the cheaper DE gas before you go home

reviews.name: The Shoppes at The Guitar Hotel
reviews.text: There’s a very high-end mall located within the Guitar Hotel is shopping is more of your vice

reviews.name: The Guitar Hotel at Seminole Hard Rock
reviews.text: A visually stunning landmark, and as this hotel is the largest thing in the very flat area, you can see it from miles away. A great place to go for a bit of a walk, whether you’re staying or not

reviews.name: Seminole Hard Rock Hotel & Casino
reviews.text: The Seminole Hard Rock Hotel is such a Fort Lauderdale (area) establishment that you can see the giant guitar and its (2010s 3rd act) skybeam as you land at the airport. …

reviews.name: Las Vegas Cuban Cuisine
reviews.text: Absolutely delicious Cuban food, with really large portions and reasonable prices. I liked my margarita (though there were no choices: frozen or shaken, or flavors), and of all the dishes, I felt that the Yuca fries were the absolute best item we ordered

reviews.name: the seed. Coffee + Juice Bar
reviews.text: A hip coffee shop with an outdoor dining area. I really enjoyed their drip coffee

reviews.name: Beach Pavilion at Lauderdale-By-The-Sea
reviews.text: The aesthetic facade which frames the beach. There’s spots here to sit, in a less sandy spot, and the foot wash stations are here

reviews.name: Lauderdale-by-the-Sea Beach
reviews.text: An exceptionally beautiful beach, which wasn’t too crowded and felt like it was largely locals. You do need to park a bit inland and walk down to the shore, but once you’re there, there’s plenty of places to grab lunch, a drink, or some coffee just off the beach

reviews.name: Publix Super Market at Dixie Crossing
reviews.location: 950 E Commercial Blvd, Oakland Park, FL 33334
reviews.text: They make a decent chicken hoagie, with a ton of fried chicken on it

reviews.name: Fort Lauderdale Fire and Safety Museum, Inc.
reviews.location: 1022 W Las Olas Blvd, Fort Lauderdale, FL 33312
reviews.text: The museum was shut when I walked by in the morning, but I still enjoyed seeing everything the museum has to offer on the exterior

reviews.name: SE 11th Ave Swing Bridge
reviews.text: When in use by cars, the 11th Ave Bridge looks completely normal. But when a ship arrives, the bridge swings itself to get out of the way, a sight to behold

reviews.name: Major William Lauderdale Park
reviews.text: For such a small park, the Major William Lauderdale Park sure does pack a mighty punch. You get not one, but two, plaques, and a fair share of funky faced birds

reviews.name: Sailboat Bend Preserve
reviews.text: The whole grass waterfront portion of Sailboat Bend is just a lovely place to go for a walk and admire the houses and the canal

reviews.name: Flanigan's Seafood Bar and Grill
reviews.text: Flanigan’s is a South Florida staple, and their green plastic cups are iconic to anyone who knows the local chain. Swing by and try the dolphin (not real dolphin meat), or the ribs, or the wings

reviews.name: Cirque du Soleil Luzia Miami
reviews.text: All Cirque du Soleil shows are spectacular, and Luzia was no different! A truly artistic and immersive experience, it was a must see while you’re in the area. All of the performers were excellent

reviews.name: Pegasus and Dragon
reviews.location: 901 S Federal Hwy, Hallandale Beach, FL 33009
reviews.text: A gigantic statue which is brightly lit up at night. You’ll pass by the statue if you’re going to the circus, or the mall complex.

reviews.name: Ann Norton Sculpture Gardens
reviews.location: 253 Barcelona Rd, West Palm Beach, FL 33401
reviews.text: Oops, all Picassos! The Ann Norton Sculpture Gardens are a bit of a misnomer, as the terrific sculptures unfortunately can’t hold a candle to all of the Picassos that they’ve accumulated in the house. They’re simply stunning, and they’ve got works across a variety of forms from the famed artist

reviews.name: 7-Eleven
reviews.location: 301 Southern Blvd, West Palm Beach, FL 33405
reviews.text: What a let down! From the outside, this 7-Eleven is so singular and elevated. But from the inside, there’s nothing special about this, and the fancier area is entirely obscured and you can’t go into the glass room. Don’t bother stopping if the outside beckons

reviews.name: Southern Boulevard Bridge Parking
reviews.text: If you’re trying to get a view of Mar-a-Lago, this is the best place to see it, from across the bay. It’s easiest to get to this parking lot by turning around and heading back from Palm Beach Island

reviews.name: Valen Grounds
reviews.location: 3065 S Dixie Hwy, West Palm Beach, FL 33405
reviews.text: Delicious drip coffee, which was comparatively cheap.

reviews.name: It's All Greek
reviews.location: 522 Belvedere Rd, West Palm Beach, FL 33405
reviews.text: In an extremely pricey neighborhood, It’s All Greek has a wide menu with a variety of reasonably priced dishes. The Greek Salad was large and very fresh, and the chicken was well cooked and flavorful
