reviews.name: Isamu Noguchi - Intetra
reviews.text: An interestingly geometric statue which is set at the end of The Four Arts’ avenue, and overlooks West Palm Beach across the short waterway

reviews.name: Garden Club of Palm Beach
reviews.location: 2 Four Arts Plaza, Palm Beach, FL 33480
reviews.text: This was the only portion of The Society of the Four Arts building complex that I was able to explore, and I found these gardens lovely. The area isn’t huge (when the rest of the gardens are shut), but you do get a few unique gardens from around the world to walk around, including a Japanese one.

reviews.name: Philip Hulitar Sculpture Garden
reviews.text: Wasn’t open when I came by, as some private event was being held there later that night. Still, the security people kept changing their rules to stop me from even looking into the main area. What a disappointment the staff here were

reviews.name: The Society of the Four Arts
reviews.location: 100 Four Arts Plaza, Palm Beach, FL 33480
reviews.text: A lovely little aesthetic building, complete with Roman style paintings at the entrance, and an elaborate, worldwide-inspired garden around the back. …

reviews.name: Worth Avenue Clock Tower
reviews.location: 423 S Ocean Blvd, Palm Beach, FL 33480
reviews.text: While the Worth Avenue Clock Tower is quite the simple structure, its location in front of the crystal blue waters makes it quite the spot to take a beautiful photo. Unfortunately, in 2026 this means that you’re going to have a lot of people doing endless, influencer-style photoshoots there.

reviews.name: The Breakers Palm Beach
reviews.location: 1 S County Rd, Palm Beach, FL 33480
reviews.text: A magnificently stunning hotel, located right on the Atlantic Ocean side of Palm Beach Island. Even if you’re not staying at the hotel, you can explore the grounds and see the impressive building and the lovely beach. You can walk from here to the Flagler museum, directly across the island

reviews.name: Historic Kapok Tree
reviews.location: 315 Chapel Hill Rd, Palm Beach, FL 33480
reviews.text: Admittedly, even as someone that seldom appreciates trees, this Kapok tree was quite impressive. Almost the starfish of trees, if I may

reviews.name: Flagler Museum
reviews.text: An exceptionally beautiful state home from a generation long gone. This house has everything from elaborate statues to an entire train car inside. When you’re on Palm Beach with some time to spare, visiting the Flagler Museum isn’t a bad way to spend it.

reviews.name: Chik Monk
reviews.location: 229 Sunrise Ave Ste C-5, Palm Beach, FL 33480
reviews.text: The drip coffee was decent, but it felt a bit pricey (that may just be PBI!)

reviews.name: McDonald's
reviews.location: 1630 S Federal Hwy, Fort Lauderdale, FL 33316
reviews.text: This McDonalds has one of the old school neon signs, with the golden arch.

reviews.name: KUBO Asian fusion and bar -Ft. lauderdale
reviews.text: A Japanese restaurant with very modern designs and stylings, that has some very good sushi. They also do events where they serve an entire tuna, which seems like a true delight

reviews.name: Cooley's Landing Marina
reviews.text: A nice spot to walk around, within the largely Sailboat Bend living area. There’s a plaque to a past tragedy, and an abundance of birds, amongst all of the boats

reviews.name: Downtown Ft Laud - Laspada's Hoagies
reviews.location: 1495 SE 17th St D, Fort Lauderdale, FL 33316
reviews.text: Delicious and gigantic hoagies, which are made to order, including slicing the meat for each order. The sandwich makers also love to throw the meat from the cutter onto the bread, which is beyond amusing. Greatly enjoyed the Italian

reviews.name: Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport
reviews.text: Not the greatest airport, but this one supports a few areas of southern Florida, from Miami to Palm Beach (though both of those places have their own airports as well). No Priority Pass lounges, but a bunch of character

reviews.name: LaGuardia Airport
reviews.text: While not the best airport in the country, much less the world, LaGuardia is most likely the best major airport supporting the NYC area. There’s a lot of lounges, including a Priority Pass-accepting Chase Lounge, and a good selection of …

reviews.name: Phillies Mural
reviews.text: What a great recent addition to the east bank of the Schuylkill River, which you can see as you drive into Center City on 76.

reviews.name: Stephen's On State
reviews.text: A fine place for dinner! Stephen’s On State has been a staple of State St. for my whole memorable life, but somehow I’ve waited more than 30 years to show up.

reviews.name: PetSmart
reviews.text: It’s a rather sizable PetSmart with a decent selection of cat, dog, bird, fish, and smaller animal supplies. They also have a fairly large number of animals housed inside

reviews.name: Wawa
reviews.text: Not the largest Wawa, but it functions great in a pinch on the way to Philly, and has all the essentials.

reviews.name: Chase Sapphire Lounge by The Club PHL
reviews.location: Philadelphia International Airport, Terminal D/E, 8500 Essington Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19153
reviews.text: The Chase Sapphire Lounge is a lovely addition to the Philly airport, with its large square footage, fancier food options, and full, complimentary drink menu. …

reviews.name: Tipsy Putt
reviews.text: Came here for a work event, and it was fine. The food wasn’t excellent (Mexican-ish), and the games were fun enough!

reviews.name: Satkar
reviews.location: 1253 W El Camino Real, Sunnyvale, CA 94087
reviews.text: A vegetarian Indian restaurant in South Bay. As someone that doesn’t eat (much) dairy, it was a tiny bit of a challenge to order here, but so many of the dishes can be made vegan, which really helped. The food was all great, and the portions were large

reviews.name: Sports Page
reviews.text: The Google bar, Building 50, B50 (it’s not a private bar). There’s trivia and a sand volleyball court and tvs in the back. …

reviews.name: Udon Mugizo
reviews.text: I’m so glad that I found Udon Mugizo because my dinner was excellent. I wanted tsukemen and they recommended the Tempura Zaru Udon, which was close enough and simply delicious. …

reviews.name: Google Gradient Canopy
reviews.location: 2000 N Shoreline Blvd, Mountain View, CA 94043
reviews.text: One of the newest Google buildings, which is inaccessible even to most of the employees who work on the larger Mountain View campus, because of the teams that sit inside

reviews.name: Haze Dispensary
reviews.text: A fine shop, they had a decent supply and a bunch of first time discounts.

reviews.name: Aloft by Marriott Mountain View
reviews.location: 840 E El Camino Real, Mountain View, CA 94040
reviews.text: A nice and convenient place to stay while on a business trip to Mountain View. I was able to check-in at 1:50am without any hassle (I did call ahead and warn that my plane was extremely delayed).

reviews.name: Duck Wall
reviews.text: There are small eccentric pieces of San Francisco which make me love this city, and Duck Wall is absolutely one of them. What wonderful weird art

reviews.name: The Painted Ladies
reviews.text: There’s a good argument to be had about where to find the nicest sunrise in SF, and Alamo Square Park, overlooking The Painted Ladies, must be near the top of any list. You can see the downtown skyscrapers of the Financial District from the park’s perch, and ships beyond in the Bay.

reviews.name: Alamo Square Park
reviews.text: Beautiful views overlooking downtown. The famous Painted Ladies are located on one leg of this park, which features the downtown skyscrapers behind it. Alamo Square Park is a lovely place to take in a sunrise

reviews.name: Sightglass Coffee
reviews.text: Some of the best coffee in the city. Never made a bad drink, and they sell some of my favorite roast beans in the Bay Area

reviews.name: Rock Spinner and Hopscotch
reviews.text: Though this area, at the end of Lawton St, isn’t quite as nice at the Sunset Dunes park area at Newton, there’s still a giant octopus, Lands End mural on the ground, and a truly imposing rock stood upright between the lanes.

reviews.name: Sunset Dunes
reviews.text: I’m so happy that SF voted to transform this portion of the road to a permanent park. It’s a beautiful space along the ocean, open to everyone

reviews.name: Lands End Lookout
reviews.location: 680 Point Lobos Ave, San Francisco, CA 94121
reviews.text: The area with all the groovy trees above Sutro Baths, which wraps around a good part of the way into the Bay towards the Golden Gate Bridge. This is one of my favorite parts of the city, I love walking through the trees, and taking in the ocean air. But be wary, it can get cold up there.

reviews.name: Avis Car Rental
reviews.location: 780 N McDonnell Rd, San Francisco, CA 94128
reviews.text: This Avis lets you pickup your car directly from the space, if you have Preferred. …

reviews.name: SFO Rental Car Center
reviews.location: 780 N McDonnell Rd, San Francisco, CA 94128
reviews.text: Apart from being located quite far aware from the airport, the SFO Rental Car Center is quite nice, has a large garage, and a decent variety of companies supported here. …

reviews.name: SFO Museum Gallery Harvey Milk Terminal 1
reviews.location: San Francisco International Airport, 8097, San Francisco, CA 94128
reviews.text: Not the largest gallery space, but there’s a few displays in a dark (and not incredibly inviting) hallway, next to Ritual coffee. It’s worth a quick visit, but certainly not worth risking missing your flight to see

reviews.name: Bun Mee SFO Terminal 3
reviews.location: San Francisco International Airport, Food Hub, Domestic Terminals Departures Level Terminal 3, San Francisco, CA 94128
reviews.text: It’s a really nice looking shop, they’re quite fast, and they’ve got nearly their whole menu from their SF locations. Unfortunately, the food is a hearty step down from the city locations.

reviews.name: San Francisco International Airport
reviews.text: Caveated by this being my home airport, this is absolutely the best airport in the country. Most of the terminals are connected on the inside. If you have TSA Precheck, waits are never longer than 10minutes, and usually only a few people. …

reviews.name: Philadelphia International Airport
reviews.text: While I’m not the biggest fan of PHL, I’ll admit that the airport has gotten quite the facelift in the past few years, and is now about as good as most of the major US airports. …

reviews.name: TJ's Grill N Chill
reviews.location: 1362 Naamans Creek Rd, Garnet Valley, PA 19060
reviews.text: A great, reasonably-priced, neighborhood greasy spoon spot for breakfast and lunch eats. The Meat Omelette had a ton of scrapple, and was very hearty for the price - the Home Fries were likewise great. The only downside is that breakfast ends at 1pm.

reviews.name: Dos Gringos Mexican Kitchen
reviews.text: I enjoyed the Tacos Mexicanos with Pork Carnitas from Dos Gringos. If you dine-in, they give you some warm, fresh (tasting) tortilla chips and salsa, and the verde was mild but nicely flavorful. …

reviews.name: La Buona Cucina
reviews.location: 1362 Naamans Creek Rd, Garnet Valley, PA 19060
reviews.text: Delicious prepackaged Italian meals, which you can freeze to make last longer.

reviews.name: AMC Lincoln Square 13
reviews.text: I’ve seen movies in a dozen states, and this has to be the coolest theatre that I’ve ever seen! On the second floor, the hallway and each theatre has been uniquely designed to reflect something related to film, Hollywood, or movie theatres. …

reviews.name: Dante West Village
reviews.text: I came to Dante with a party of 20 for a large work event, and they had customized the menu for us, which was pretty unique and a very nice touch. Then the food was absolutely delicious, the chicken was so well cooked, but really everything …

reviews.name: M&M'S New York
reviews.text: The M&M store in Times Square is something of a tourist attraction, as there’s mascots, apparel, and signage recognizing the prominent location, but if you’re not trying to buy some chocolate or a souvenir, there’s little to see or do

reviews.name: Chelsea Market
reviews.text: A block-long food market with a wide variety of permanent vendors, and a mix of other shops. There’s often some cool displays detailing older NYC of years past, and to the history of the building, which was once a biscuit factory.

reviews.name: Grand Bazaar NYC
reviews.text: A weekly market with dozens of vendors arranged in a tennis court, expanding into a high school gymnasium. There were mainly clothing, goods, and art stands, with a food section by the entrance and free Vitamin Water samples.

reviews.name: The Viand
reviews.text: While The Viand isn’t an old-school NYC diner, they still get the job done when you’re in need of a breakfast. They’ve got quite large omelettes for a fair price, which come with homemade jam. The coffee was fine

reviews.name: Gray's Papaya
reviews.text:
Gray’s Papaya is an institution of the Upper West
Side, most notably for their hot dogs and their papaya juice, but they also sell quite tasty breakfast sandwiches which are only $3 with a cup of coffee. …

reviews.name: AMC 84th Street 6
reviews.text: One of the smaller AMC theatres in the city, and while they don’t have any larger format screens here (no IMAX or Dolby), they do have the fancy recliners; so you get comfort over the visual resolution.

reviews.name: 7th Street Burger
reviews.text: A good place to stop and get a good, greasy smash burger and some fries. The burgers were better than the fries, and same as with Five Guys, you’ll likely want to get a double if you’re an adult. …

reviews.name: El Gallo Taqueria
reviews.text: An option for pretty solid Mexican food for a rather reasonable price  The Carne Asada bowl was decent, and I really like their tacos, with the Carne Asada being a bit better than the Al Pastor

reviews.name: Chopt Creative Salad Co.
reviews.location: Moynihan Train Hall Food Court, 383 W 31st St Ste 037, New York, NY 10001
reviews.text: A great option for a lunch on the go. The salads were reasonably priced and extremely portable. I’d definitely recommend the Greek Salad and adding Chicken, you also get free bread.

reviews.name: The Met Cloisters
reviews.location: 99 Margaret Corbin Dr, New York, NY 10040
reviews.text: The Met Cloisters is situated atop a hill at the very tippy top of Manhattan, and serves as something of a prize for venturing up to the sleepier portion of the island. …

reviews.name: Citi Field
reviews.text: Citi Field is home of the New York Mets, and they also use the stadium for some corporate events and concerts. It’s a great venue with a good variety of vendors. …

reviews.name: The Strand
reviews.text: Some book stores have this calming ambiance and The Strand has that in heaps. An extremely expansive bookstore with a children’s section in the basement.

reviews.name: Brickman's Columbus Ave
reviews.text: An extremely densely packed hardware store that’s likely got what you’re looking for. There were a number of employees ready to help me as well.

reviews.name: Crumbl Cookies
reviews.text: The national gourmet, giant cookie and cake chain. Their desserts are good, but certainly more of a treat, or a gift, than a regular item. …

reviews.name: Moynihan Food Hall
reviews.text: The Moynihan Food Hall (within Penn Station) has a surprisingly wide selection of restaurants to choose from before you catch your train.

reviews.name: Broad Nosh Bagels
reviews.text: One of the better bagel options in the UWS, though don’t get the salt bagel. It was entirely covered in rock salt and way overly done. …

reviews.name: Spring St
reviews.text: A decent station. Nothing fancy, and nothing artsy, but it gets the job done. There’s an underpass to get to the other direction trains.

reviews.name: 7 Hudson Square
reviews.text: 7 Hudson Square is the new home of Disney in New York, both the corporate offices, and the studio spaces living within the building. In the mornings, you can see celebrities entering and exiting the building for their media obligations, and upstairs there’s a theatre for employee only screenings, and a Starbucks

reviews.name: Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis Reservoir
reviews.text: The Reservoir is the largest body of water in Central Park and one of its most notable landmarks. You can’t go out onto the water, and you certainly can’t swim in it. There is a running track that goes along the perimeter of the body of water, which enforces a single direction of traffic, counter-clockwise.

reviews.name: The Lake
reviews.text: There’s a few bodies of water within Central Park and The Lake is one of the more prominent ones, although not the largest. But for The Pond, it’s the most downtown body of water, so it gives some of the best reflected skyscraper views. You can also see the Dakota and other iconic UWS buildings from here.

reviews.name: Swingers NoMad
reviews.text: A very expansive, indoor miniature golf place, with multiple courses located on the property. It’s a very aesthetically pleasing place, with colorful lights, and good scenes for photography. They also have decent food and drinks. I came here for a work event and we all had a great time

reviews.name: Times Square Diner & Grill
reviews.text: I was trying to get brunch somewhere else in the neighborhood, but they were crowded, so I came to the Times Square Diner and they were fine. The Strawberry Nutella Pancakes were really the standout, with the omelettes and home fries both just being fine. I didn’t love the coffee.

reviews.name: Peace Fountain by Greg Wyatt
reviews.text: The Peace Fountain may be my singular favorite statue in the whole of New York City. There’s so much going on, it’s chaotic, it’s messy, it’s fantastic. It’s surrounded by a ring of smaller animal statues, complimenting the animal parts that encompass the larger artwork.

reviews.name: H&H Bagels
reviews.location: Moynihan Train Hall, 421 8th Ave, New York, NY 10199
reviews.text: The H&H in Penn Station is located between the main atrium of the Moynihan Train Hall and the Food Court, and while there’s often a line, it does move quickly. This is a fair place to grab a breakfast before heading on your train, or a black and white cookie as a gift.

reviews.name: City Diner
reviews.text: A large square-footage diner with a bar counter, an old timey feel, and some good pancakes. A friend and I got two Egg dishes (an Omelette and Eggs), and an order of Chocolate Chip Pancakes, and the cakes were by far the standout. Also didn’t love the house coffee.

reviews.name: Tom's Restaurant
reviews.text: Let’s be real, you’re not coming to Tom’s for the food, you’re coming here because of the show. And while Tom’s certainly caters to the fans by having a number of pictures of the cast, it’s functionally just a typical NYC diner. The Lumberjack was pretty decent

reviews.name: Kossar's Bagels & Bialys
reviews.text: Kossar’s makes an excellent breakfast sandwich, I went with my typical Sausage, Egg, and Cheese on an Everything Bagel, and I loved what I got. They brew La Colombe coffee, and my only complaint is that their cups are horrible; it still leaked through two cups

reviews.name: Hall of Saurischian Dinosaurs
reviews.text: One of my favorite parts of the History Museum, filled with Dinosaurs stretching across vast halls, and towering over crowds. But be wary, this is also one of the busiest parts of the building, with a heavy density of people filling every nook and cranny.

reviews.name: Horace Greeley Monument
reviews.location: 894-900 Ave Of The Amer, New York, NY 10001
reviews.text: Horace has the misfortune of having both an old looking face and an old sounding name. At least they gave the old guy a chair to spend eternity in. They’ve also surrendered him with flowers, making the whole thing look almost like a tomb. RIP Ol’ Horace

reviews.name: Carl Schurz Park
reviews.location: East 86th Street &, East End Ave, New York, NY 10028
reviews.text: Carl Schurz Park is located on the East River in the Upper East Side, and contains a section of John Finley walk and Gracie Mansion. There’s also a Peter Pan Statue and a lot of green shrubbery, it’s a fine place to go for a break or a bit of a walk.

reviews.name: Penn Station
reviews.text: NY Penn Station has a worse reputation than it deserves. As someone that regularly uses Amtrak, I really like the aesthetic design of the station, the availability of the subways underneath, and the selection of restaurants and shops and their hours.

reviews.name: Schmackary's
reviews.text: Somehow NYC has a bunch of competing gourmet cookie chains. Schmackary’s is a delicious offering, with more reasonably sized cookies, which were all named after Broadway shows. I got the Book of Mormon one, which was great. I’ll be back to try more.

reviews.name: The Ravine
reviews.text: There’s a few areas of Central Park where you can get deep enough into the green to forget that you’re still in the heart of the largest city in the country. The Ravine is one of those places, which makes it one of my favorite parts of the megacity

reviews.name: Eleanor Roosevelt Memorial
reviews.text: Eleanor Roosevelt was the first female aviatrix to fly across the Pacific Ocean, until everything changed when she vanished one day from her house never to be seen again. People have searched everywhere for her plane, but no one knows where it went

reviews.name: Läderach
reviews.text: A gourmet chocolatier with a higher price point which makes decent gifts for loved ones. The store has a human-sized statue of liberty made out of chocolate inside, and heaps of sheets of chocolate. They also tend to give out free samples as well.

reviews.name: Sutton Park
reviews.text: There’s really three attractions in Sutton Park, first the stunning views of the Queensboro Bridge. Then there’s quite a nice statue to a boar in a greener portion of the park. And finally, there’s the views of the Eastern portions of the city.

reviews.name: Morningside Park
reviews.text: While not as famous as Central Park or Riverside Park, Morningside Park is one of Manhattans great parks. Located above Central Park on the westside, this park offers a number of steep, hilly paths, and a serene lake with a purported waterfall.

reviews.name: Times Square
reviews.text: Times Square is arguably the most famous place in New York City, and in turn, maybe the most consistently busy. There’s a ton to see, from people watching, to taking in the thousands of neon adverts blaring, there’s much to see in Times Square

reviews.name: Porto Rico Importing Co.
reviews.text: One of the best smelling shops in NYC, with endless burlap sacks full of roast coffee beans, and their beans are largely quite good. There’s staff that can walk you through choosing the right beans for your tastes, and they also have all of …

reviews.name: Central Park
reviews.text: NYC’s iconic park, and one of the largest urban parks in the world, Central Park is the home to multiple bodies of water, horse stables, and fantastic views of the large residential buildings that line the sides, and skyscrapers at its base.

reviews.name: Inwood Hill Park
reviews.location: Payson Ave. &, Seaman Ave, New York, NY 10034
reviews.text: If you’re looking for the furthest north point in Manhattan, you’ve found it! Inwood Hill Park sits at the northwest corner of the island, and is equally dense with trees and sparse with humans (on the ground). Though you can nearly always …

reviews.name: Gracie Mansion Conservancy
reviews.location: 181 East End Ave, New York, NY 10128
reviews.text: Honestly, I didn’t realize that Gracie Mansion was located here when I was intending to see Peter Pan, but this was something of a nice surprise. You really can’t get up close to the building at all, which makes sense, for security purposes.

reviews.name: Google NYC - Chelsea Market
reviews.text: Google purchased the entirety of the historic Chelsea Market building more than a decade ago, and while the public floors haven’t been updated, the upper (employee only) floors are really quite exquisite, and one of the more interesting …

reviews.name: Bareburger
reviews.text: I really enjoyed Bareburger, they’re a slightly more elevated NYC burger chain, with a bit of a higher price point, which gets you a higher quality burger, with more fun accoutrements. It’s also a sit down restaurant, which caught me by …

reviews.name: Non-Violence - Carl Fredrik Reuterswärd
reviews.location: United Nations Secretariat Building, 405 E 42nd St, New York, NY 10017
reviews.text: I’m certain Non-Violence is a better statue than I’ve reviewed it, but it’s so inaccessible from the street, it’s a true shame. Art shouldn’t be hidden behind walls, and I’d assume the UN (of all organizations) that should understand that

reviews.name: Just Salad
reviews.text: Great salads, and they come with free rosemary-y bread. They have a whole array of precurated options, and you can swap out any ingredients that you want. Just Salad also has a rewards program in you get their app, or go on the website. …

reviews.name: 190 St
reviews.text: Quite an interesting metro station. The signage at the upper level is cool and retro, however you have to take an elevator down from there. There’s another entrance, at the ground level, but no stairs or escalators to get you down there

reviews.name: Mount Tom
reviews.text: Less of a mountain and more of a big honking rock, you can climb Mount Tom and get a decent overview of the Warsaw Monument, but on account of the heavy tree cover, not much else. Still, it’s a fun place to do a bit of rock scrambling.

reviews.name: Church of the Heavenly Rest
reviews.text: An exceptionally stunning single-halled church. Cast with white stone calls, and elaborate stained glass panels lining three of the side, the Church of the Heavenly Rest exudes beauty from every pew and from under each and every arch.

reviews.name: St. Frances Cabrini Shrine
reviews.location: 701 Fort Washington Ave, New York, NY 10040
reviews.text: St. Frances Cabrini Shrine is a church, so if you’re visiting on a Sunday, there will be services going on. There was a front area with a gift shop-appearing section, that was cool even if I didn’t get to see the rest of the building

reviews.name: General Grant National Memorial
reviews.location: W 122nd St &, Riverside Dr, New York, NY 10027
reviews.text: The General Grant Memorial has a few unique things going for it. Maybe most notable is the mosaic bench that stretches around the perimeter of the building. Closely followed by Grant’s tomb which is just a bit north of the building.

reviews.name: American Museum of Natural History
reviews.text: Certainly one of the best Natural History Museums in the country, if not the world. Regardless of which animal, vegetable, or mineral you’re hoping to see, it’s likely in this museum. My favorite exhibits were the butterflies, the …

reviews.name: Blue Bottle Coffee
reviews.text: When you’re in Penn Station and need a quick cup of coffee, or a pastry, Blue Bottle isn’t a bad option. They’re situated right in the main atrium of the Moynihan Train Hall, which is super convenient for those commuting via train.
